1.w: I speak truth in Christ—I am not lying, my conscience is testifying with me in the Holy Spirit

2.w: that sorrow to me is great, and unceasing pain [is] in my heart.

3.w: For I could wish myself to be accursed, apart from Christ for my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh,

4.w: who are Israelites, whose [is] the adoption as sons and the glory and the covenants and the lawgiving and the service and the promises,

5.w: whose [are] the fathers, and from whom [is] Christ according to the flesh, being God over all, blessed to the ages! Amen.

6.w: But [it is] not as though the word of God has failed. For not all who [are] of Israel, [are] these Israel.

7.w: Nor because they are seed of Abraham [are] all children. Rather, “In Isaac a seed will be called to you.”

8.w: That is, the children of the flesh, these [are] not children of God; but the children of the promise are reckoned for seed.

9.w: For this [is] the word of promise: “At this time I will come, and to Sarah there will be a son.”

10.w: And not only [so], but also Rebecca, having conception by one, Isaac our father—

11.w: for they not yet having been born nor having done anything good or evil, so that the purpose of God according to election might stand—

12.w: not of works but of the One calling, it was said to her, “The greater will serve the lesser.”

13.w: As it has been written: “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”

14.w: What then will we say? [Is there] injustice with God? Never may it be!

15.w: For He says to Moses: “I will have mercy on whom I may have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I may have compassion.”

16.w: So then, [it is] not of the one willing, nor of the one running, but of God having mercy.

17.w: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: “For this very thing I raised you up, so that I might display My power in you, and that My name should be declared in all the earth.”

18.w: So then, He has mercy on whom He wants, and He hardens whom He wants.

19.w: You will say, then, to me, “Why then does He still find fault? For who has resisted His will?”

20.w: But rather, O man, who are you answering against God? [Will] the thing formed say to the One having formed [it], “Why did you make me thus?”

21.w: Or does the potter not have authority over the clay to make out of the same lump the one vessel indeed for honor, but the one for dishonor?

22.w: And [what] if God, desiring to display the wrath and to make known His power, bore with much patience vessels of wrath, having been fitted for destruction,

23.w: so that He might also make known the riches of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared beforehand for glory,

24.w: even us, whom He called not only out from Jews, but also out from Gentiles?

25.w: As He also says in Hosea: “I will call that which [is] not My people ‘My People,’ and her not beloved ‘Beloved,’”

26.w: and, “It will be [that] in the place where it was said to them, ‘You⁺ [are] not My people,’ there they will be called ‘sons of the living God.””

27.w: And Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: “Though the number of the sons of Israel may be like the sand of the sea, [only] the remnant will be saved.

28.w: For the Lord will execute [His] word, finishing and accomplishing swiftly upon the earth.”

29.w: And, as Isaiah forewarned: “Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us a seed, we would have become like Sodom, and we would have been made like Gomorrah.”

30.w: What then will we say? That the Gentiles, not pursuing righteousness, obtained righteousness—and righteousness that [is] by faith;

31.w: but Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, did not attain to [that] law.

32.w: Why? Because [it was] not by faith, but as by works. They stumbled over the stone of stumbling,

33.w: as it has been written: “Behold, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; and the one believing on Him will not be put to shame.”
